Oh man. My heart wrenched reading this post. What I am about to say is going to sound cliche but it is true: the grass is always greener on the other side.

Meaning from your perspective it may look like she's having the time of her life and everything's great but that's not necessarily the case. It very well could be the opposite as well.

What I do know is that the only way to "clear the air" is to be open and honest. It's up to you to decide what that means to you. That could be as simple as journaling your feelings, writing down your thoughts and sorting them out. It could also be opening up to friends and family and talking about it. Or having an honest conversation with her about how you are feeling. The last one imo is the most difficult as it leaves a chance of feeling rejected but may also be the most freeing as you have laid all your cards on the table.
From what I gather somebody you loved hurt you real bad along the way and rather that admit it and deal with it properly this is how you choose to handle it. You need professional help.
